name: Nitrification (Ammonia Oxidation)
notes: Aerobic ammonia oxidation pathway: ammonia → hydroxylamine → nitrite → nitrate. Used by ammonia-oxidizing bacteria (AOB) and archaea (AOA) for chemolithoautotrophic growth. Note: pmoA-amoA genes are homologous - same gene used in both methanotrophy and ammonia oxidation.

genes.name: ammonia monooxygenase subunit A
genes.notes: Catalytic subunit of ammonia monooxygenase. Highly conserved marker for nitrification. Note: Gene name pmoA-amoA in GATOR reflects homology with methane monooxygenase.

genes.name: ammonia monooxygenase complex
genes.notes: Three-subunit ammonia monooxygenase. Oxidizes NH3 to NH2OH.

genes.name: hydroxylamine dehydrogenase
genes.notes: Oxidizes hydroxylamine to nitrite. Unique to nitrifying organisms. Diagnostic marker.

genes.name: nitrate reductase / nitrite oxidoreductase, alpha subunit
genes.notes: In nitrification context, acts as nitrite oxidoreductase (reverse direction). Oxidizes nitrite to nitrate.

genes.name: nitrate reductase / nitrite oxidoreductase, beta subunit
nitrite oxidoreductase complex
genes.notes: Two-subunit nitrite oxidoreductase (reverse of nitrate reductase). Note: narI not required for this direction.

nitrification.name: Nitrification (Complete)
nitrification.notes: Three-step ammonia oxidation pathway. Step 1: NH3 → NH2OH (amoABC). Step 2: NH2OH → NO2- (hao). Step 3: NO2- → NO3- (narGH). Note: Some nitrifiers only perform partial pathway (AOB stop at nitrite, NOB oxidize nitrite to nitrate). This potato represents complete nitrification.

scoring.notes: amoA and hao are diagnostic markers. narGH may be absent (partial nitrifiers). Allow 1 gap for AOB lacking nitrite oxidation.
